deep.reconstruction:
Context: Hilbert notebook, c. 1902 (the previous page cites a 1902 lecture). The page refers back to his own lecture notes 'Kugelfunktionen' 1887/88, p. 41.

Problem. Find polynomials P (deg n, simple zeros, P(±1)≠0) such that ∫ dx/((x²−1)P²) has no logarithmic terms other than log(x+1) and log(x−1). Equivalently, in the partial fraction decomposition of 1/((x²−1)P²), each zero α of P contributes only a double-pole term A/(x−α)². It contributes no simple-pole term a/(x−α), so the residue is 0.

Step 1. Local condition at each zero α of P:
1/((x²−1)P²) = A/(x−α)² + 𝔓(x−α), where 𝔓 is a power series in (x−α).

Step 2. Invert. Put g = (x²−1)P². Then
g = (x−α)²/(A + (x−α)²𝔓) = (1/A)(x−α)² + (x−α)⁴𝔓₁(x−α).   (I)
So the vanishing residue is equivalent to g having no (x−α)³ term, i.e. g'''(α) = 0.

Step 3. Since this holds at every (simple) zero of P, P divides d³[(x²−1)P²]/dx³. This is the form recorded in the 1887/88 lecture notes.

Step 4 (marginal improvement). The cleaner form is that ((x²−1)P')' must be divisible by P. Hilbert says this follows from (I) by differentiating and dividing by P, giving (x²−1)P' = c + (x−α)²𝔓(x−α).
- My verification, with h = x²−1: since P(α)=0, (P²)'(α)=0, (P²)''(α)=2P'(α)², (P²)'''(α)=6P'(α)P''(α).
- Hence g'''(α) = 6h'P'² + 6hP'P'' = 6P'(α)·(hP')'(α).
- As P'(α)≠0, the condition is (hP')'(α)=0, i.e. hP' = c + O((x−α)²), exactly the marginal claim.
- My completion (not on the page): deg((x²−1)P')' = n, so ((x²−1)P')' = λP. Comparing leading coefficients gives λ = n(n+1). This is Legendre's equation, so P = const·P_n.

Step 5 (program). Hilbert notes that one sees directly in this way that the P_n are the convergent denominators of the continued fraction for ½ log((x+1)/(x−1)). The next page has ∫_∞^x dx/((x²−1)P_n²) = −Q_n/P_n and Q_n = P_n·½log((x+1)/(x−1)) − Z_n. He calls the idea capable of great generalization, in two directions:
(a) as indicated in the 1887/88 notes;
(b) by simultaneous continued fractions, approximating several different functions with one common denominator P.
Tasks he sets himself:
- Prove the rational approximation of e^x this way.
- Develop the Bessel function into a continued fraction, i.e. approximate it by rational functions. His footnote: so as finally to obtain irrationality proofs for Bessel function values at rational arguments.
- Connect with Abel's work (Œuvres I p.104, the memoir on ∫ρdx/√R, and II pp. 87(?)–188), where periodic continued fractions arise.
- Note related questions in the modern theory of eigen-oscillations (Eigenschwingungen).
errors: No substantive error. The marginal 'better' derivation is stated tersely. Differentiating (I) and dividing by P gives 2(x²−1)P' + 2xP = (2/A)/u + O((x−α)²), with P = (x−α)u. Reaching (x²−1)P' = c + O((x−α)²) needs a further computation of the linear coefficient, using 1/A = h(α)P'(α)². That computation does yield (hP')'(α)=0, so the claim is right but not as immediate as suggested.
Implicit assumptions: P has only simple zeros, and P(±1)≠0. These are needed for 'P divides g'''' and for the residue argument; unstated but harmless.
In (I) the coefficient 1/A is correct only to leading order: the series written after it is a different series 𝔓₁, reusing the same symbol 𝔓 loosely.

results.what: Characterization of Legendre polynomials: ∫dx/((x²−1)P²) has no logarithmic terms except log(x±1) iff P divides d³[(x²−1)P²]/dx³ iff P divides ((x²−1)P')', i.e. P satisfies Legendre's equation
results.modern_name: Residue-free (no log terms) characterization of Legendre polynomials; Christoffel–Heine representation Q_n = P_n∫_x^∞dt/((t²−1)P_n²)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical 19th c. (Heine, Handbuch der Kugelfunctionen; Christoffel); cf. Heine I pp.137–138, cited on the next page

results.what: P_n are the denominators of the continued fraction (Padé) convergents of ½log((x+1)/(x−1))
results.modern_name: Padé approximants / Gauss continued fraction for the logarithm; Legendre polynomials as orthogonal-polynomial denominators

results.what: Program: generalize via simultaneous continued fractions (one common denominator for several functions), applied to e^x and to Bessel functions, aiming at irrationality of Bessel values at rational arguments
results.modern_name: Hermite–Padé (simultaneous) approximation as a tool for irrationality/transcendence; precursor of Siegel's E-function method
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite (1873, e); Padé (1890s); Siegel (1929, Bessel values); Mahler (1930s, Hermite–Padé theory)

results.what: Link with Abel's pseudo-elliptic integrals and periodic continued fractions
results.modern_name: Abel–Chebyshev polynomial Pell equation / periodic continued fractions of √R

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page (Legendre polynomials from the vanishing of residues, Padé denominators) is classical. Notable is the c.1902 research program: simultaneous continued fractions (Hermite–Padé) to approximate e^x and Bessel functions, explicitly aiming at irrationality of Bessel values at rational points. This anticipates the circle of ideas Siegel realized in 1929 and Mahler systematized. It is a sketch of intentions, not a result, and Hilbert's interest in Hermite-type transcendence methods is well known. So it is a notable unpublished detail, not a major priority claim.

checkable.sympy: x=symbols('x'); P=legendre(3,x); [residue(1/((x**2-1)*P**2), x, r) for r in solve(P,x)] == [0,0,0]
checkable.asserts: 1/((x²−1)P_n²) has zero residue at each zero of P_n (no log terms besides log(x±1))

checkable.sympy: x,a,b,c=symbols('x a b c'); P=x**3+a*x**2+b*x+c; sol=solve(Poly(rem(expand(diff((x**2-1)*diff(P,x),x)), P, x), x).all_coeffs(), [a,b,c], dict=True); sol
checkable.asserts: The monic cubic with P | ((x²−1)P')' is P = x³ − (3/5)x, i.e. a=0, b=−3/5, c=0, proportional to Legendre P_3

transcription_corrections: Final line 'Theorie der Eigenschwi-' continues on the next page as 'Eigenschwingungen' ('Auch in der modernen Theorie der Eigenschwingungen handelt es sich ja um anklingende Fragen').
'mehrerer verschiedener Funktion' should probably read 'mehrerer verschiedener Funktionen'.

Marginal insertion reads: 'Besser aber findet man aus (I) direkt durch Differentiation nach x und Division mit P, dass (x²−1)P' = c+(x−α)²𝔓(x−α) sein muss und folglich [((x²−1)P')' durch P teilbar sein muss]'. The circled note '((x²−1)P')' durch P teilbar sein muss' completes this sentence rather than following (I).
Before 1/A in (I) a struck-out symbol stands (rendered [-...-]); the right-hand side is (1/A)(x−α)² + (x−α)⁴𝔓(x−α).
Abel reference: 'Werke Bd 1 S. 104 und Bd 2 S. 87–188' as written. The second page range may be '187–188'; the reading is uncertain.
